physical_subject: Why can a network with seven units of entry and exit capacity carry only six?
relationship: A cut with capacity six bounds every feasible flow, and an explicit six-unit routing proves optimality; increasing its middle edge permits seven.
operation: Keep one directed network throughout: expose a separating cut, construct a routing that attains its bound, then increase the binding internal edge.
closest_prior: Dijkstra shortest path, traveling salesman, Braess paradox, single-machine scheduling and hydraulic leverage
substantive_difference: An attained cut bound proves maximum throughput in a directed capacity network; not shortest distance, selfish traffic equilibrium, completion-time ordering or hydraulic force.
